How it Works


Team Selection

The eight players on each team can earn entry into the field through a variety of ways:

Captain

Each Skechers World Champions Cup supporting Shriners Children’s Captain will be a playing Captain, working hand in hand with the Vice Captains on the overall competition for their team.

Vice Captain

The Vice Captains serve in a non-playing role and strategically assists Captains with pairings and overall competition planning for the week.

Automatic Qualifier

The top two-point earners for each team will receive automatic invitations based on the Skechers World Champions Cup supporting Shriners Children’s Historical Rankings. These points are based on prior wins on the PGA TOUR, DP World Tour and PGA TOUR Champions as well as team-based event participation.

Chairman Selection

The Chairman of the tournament will select two players for each team. 

Play-in Positions

A final spot on each team will be filled based on the season-ending Charles Schwab Cup standings and treated as a play in spot. If the first player, per team, who qualifies through this position is already in the field, then the next applicable player in the standings will be chosen.



Format

The Skechers World Champions Cup supporting Shriners Children’s is a three-team, stroke-play team competition that will be contested across 24 nine-hole groupings featuring team and singles play. The team formats will be Six Ball and Scotch Sixsomes (Modified Alternate Shot) with morning and afternoon waves.  

Scotch Sixsome

In Scotch Sixsome, both players in each two-man team will tee off on every hole. One ball is chosen and then alternate strokes are then played to complete the hole. The team with the lowest score on each hole will receive two points. The team with the second lowest score on a hole will receive one point. The team with the highest score will receive no points. Whenever teams finish with the same score on a hole, those teams will be awarded the same number of points.

Six Ball

In Six Ball, each member of a two-man team plays his own ball, so six golf balls are in play on every hole. Each team counts the lowest of its two scores on each hole, and the team with the lowest score on each hole will receive two points. The team with the second lowest score on a hole will receive one point. The team with the highest score will receive no points. Whenever teams finish with the same score on a hole, those teams will be awarded the same number of points.

Singles

In singles, each grouping features one player from each team. The player with the lowest score on each hole will receive two points. The player with the second lowest score on a hole will receive one point. The player with the highest score will receive no points. Whenever players finish with the same score on a hole, those teams will be awarded the same number of points. 


Scoring

A total of three points will be awarded on each hole and based on each team’s individual result. Each team must complete each hole and as a result all groupings will be played in their entirety (nine holes). There are no close outs or concessions.

Points

The team with the lowest score on each hole will receive two points. The team with the second lowest score on a hole will receive one point. The team with the highest score will receive no points. Whenever teams finish with the same score on a hole, those teams will be awarded the same number of points.  In the event that two teams finish with the lowest score on a hole, each team will receive one and a half points. The third team, finishing with the highest score will receive no points. In the event that all three times finish with the same score on a hole, each team will receive one point.

PURSE - $1.35 MILLION 

1st Place - $100,000 per player | 2nd Place - $75,000 per player | 3rd Place - $50,000 per player
